title: 'I'm going to shoot you': 2 men held at gunpoint before deputies realize their mistake, victims say

reading.body:
This is a false positive from an automated vehicle alert that was escalated into an armed stop. A camera system flagged a stolen Camaro, and deputies treated the flag as an identification rather than as a lead. The stop was carried out with guns drawn and handcuffs before anyone confirmed the vehicle was the one being sought.

The failure sits at the handoff between the alert and the stop. The plate was the field that could have distinguished the flagged car from any other Camaro, and neither the deputies nor the helicopter could read it. The identification therefore rested on make and model alone, which is not enough to single out one vehicle, and the stop went forward anyway.

Catching this would have required confirming the plate before the stop rather than after it, or treating an unconfirmed alert as a reason to hold back. The sheriff's office says supervisors will review body camera video to check whether procedures were followed, and both men plan to file internal affairs complaints. Whether the deputies followed procedure is not established, the account of the threat to shoot is the men's allegation, and no finding has been made against anyone.

reports.title: 'I'm going to shoot you': 2 men held at gunpoint before deputies realize their mistake, victims say

summary:
On Aug. 3 in Cypress, Texas, Harris County sheriff's deputies mistook two 19-year-old men, Anthony and Julian, for car thieves. Deputies surrounded Anthony's Camaro with at least five patrol cars and a helicopter, pointed guns, handcuffed them, and one deputy threatened to shoot, according to the men. Flock cameras had flagged a stolen Camaro linked to aggravated robberies, but deputies and the helicopter could not read the plates. After handcuffing them, deputies realized it was the wrong car. The men were not charged.

Anthony's mother, Leslie, wants deputies held accountable and plans to hire an attorney. The sheriff's office says supervisors, including the district captain, shift lieutenants, and shift sergeants, will review body worn camera video to check whether procedures were followed. The men were told how to file a formal complaint with internal affairs, and both plan to do so.
title_en: 'I'm going to shoot you': 2 men held at gunpoint before deputies realize their mistake, victims say
